headlines.summary: OKXICE is set to debut Monday despite objections from 90% of the companies whose stocks it initially proposed to list.
headlines.article_text: Tokenized stocks face pushback as NYSE, Nasdaq pivot for a new market Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points OKXICE launches Monday with Coinbase, Robinhood, Strategy, Circle, Securitize and BitGo will be available to trade in tokenized form. Most of the 62 companies initially targeted objected to having their shares tokenized on the platform, likely reflecting a lack of preparedness versus a rejection of tokenization. Company objections raise a separate question about which of the different tokenization models will prove most attractive. In this article ICE Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Traders work on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York City, Nov. 10, 2026. Angela Weiss | AFP | Getty Images OKXICE, a trading platform for tokenized securities jointly operated by Intercontinental Exchange and crypto exchange OKX, is set to debut Monday despite objections from 90% of the companies whose stocks it initially proposed to list. Of the 62 companies whose shares OKXICE first sought to trade, 56 objected to having their shares tokenized and traded on the platform, according to a review of public notices posted between Oct. 4 and Nov. 5 . By last week, even more companies had objected , including those not on the original roster. The high objection rate may reflect companies' lack of readiness to have blockchain-based representations of their shares traded on a new third-party platform like OKXICE, rather than broad resistance to tokenization. People involved in talks with some of the companies say a 30-day objection window left them little time to react and decide if they were ready to participate. 'Revolutionary,' 'transformational' "The shift to a 24/7 global marketplace is revolutionary and transformational for our market structure," Andrew Cuomo, co-chair of OKXICE, told CNBC. "The majority of companies aren't familiar with [tokenization] and haven't had a chance to understand it and the consequences." "Logic dictates that many companies were going to be cautious before they understood what the system would do," added Cuomo, who served 10 years as governor of New York until 2021. "What you're seeing now is the more the companies learn about 24/7 global access, the more receptive they are." At launch, tokenized shares of Coinbase , Robinhood , Strategy , Circle , Securitize and BitGo will be available to trade on the platform, OKXICE disclosed in a public notice. OKXICE has confirmed 113 assets, including exchange-traded funds and products, going live on a rolling basis. Since its initial pre-launch announcement on Nov. 11, OKXICE said it's seen further interest from different issuers and Fidelity Investments , Direxion, eToro , Strive and Vida Global are now participating. The 30-day opt-out window is a requirement of the SEC's so-called Innovation Exemption , which took effect in September and temporarily permits the trading of certain tokenized stocks. Under the exemption, trading platforms must notify the underlying issuers and give them an opportunity to object. Any issuer who objects blocks its shares from being tokenized. "We've gotten a lot of feedback that the reason why you've seen this high number of rejections of tokenizing equity is because it was a 30-day window," Seth Ginns, chief investment officer at Franklin Templeton's crypto arm, told CNBC at the Digital Assets Forum in New York earlier this month. Many issuers were open to exploring the idea but were hesitant to move forward amid competing priorities, he said. "[They're] saying it's earnings season, there was the midterms, there's a lot going on during this 30-day window. Give us some time, we want to learn about it, we're not closed to the idea we're just closed to rushing into it right now," Ginns added. Announcement timing Ran Grushkowsky, CEO of MassPay, a global payout platform, said several of his company's clients were among the initial targets and shared that their concern was less about the concept of tokenization and more about how 24/7 trading could affect stock value and investor relations strategies, particularly around the timing of corporate announcements. "It's more [about] what's going to be the effect, how is it going to actually drive the value of the stock," he said. "A lot of the strategy that happens around investors relations has to do with scheduling and when you announce certain things and so how do you do it when your stock is being traded 24/7?" watch now VIDEO 2:22 02:22 Why Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo expects more companies to embrace tokenization efforts Crypto "The executives were actually quite excited about this new innovation and potentially getting more interest into the stock. It was really from the [investor relations] side that they received push back," and heard "let's hold off," Grushkowsky added. The lack of awareness may even extend to executives overseeing digital asset initiatives, suggesting that some rejections stem from internal communication gaps and unfamiliarity with the process, according to Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo, whose company is one of the first being listed on OKX. Securitize is also the tokenization partner for OKX. "We've talked to some of the issuers that have opted out [where] the head of digital assets doesn't even know who in the company rejected them," he said. "This is a consequence of, first, the novelty of the process and of these venues, and second, the lack of understanding of what they're being notified to do." watch now VIDEO 3:05 03:05 Robinhood CEO on tokenization: It allows us to distribute access to U.S. stocks globally Squawk Box Despite the initial pushback, Domingo expects more issuers to participate as companies become more familiar with the model, noting that some regulated trading venues can operate without issuer consent. Long game Company objections raise a separate question about which of the different tokenization models will prove most attractive. The main alternative to the OKXICE model is an issuer-led approach that integrates blockchain-based shares into existing regulated market infrastructures, with issuers retaining greater control over the process. Bullish, a digital asset platform, is pursuing an example of this model through its partnership with Equiniti, the transfer-agent business it's acquiring for $4 billion . headlines.summary: Netflix’s "The Altruists" has drawn backlash over its portrayal of the FTX collapse, with prominent crypto industry figures questioning the series’ accuracy
headlines.article_text: Netflix’s ‘The Altruists’ sparks debates over depiction of FTX collapse Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Netflix’s portrayal of the FTX collapse has drawn criticism from Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao and other crypto industry figures. The series misrepresents the roles of key figures in the FTX scandal, critics say. Netflix has previously faced defamation lawsuits over its portrayals of real-life figures in "Inventing Anna" and "Baby Reindeer." In this article NFLX Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT NEW YORK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 19: (L-R) Anthony Boyle, Julia Garner and Graham Moore attend Netflix's "The Altruists" New York Premiere at The Plaza Hotel on November 19, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Arturo Holmes/WireImage) Arturo Holmes | Wireimage | Getty Images Netflix's "The Altruists," released Nov. 19, has sparked backlash from prominent cryptocurrency industry figures, including Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao, over its portrayal of the collapse of FTX. Critics have questioned the accuracy of the series' portrayal of the FTX collapse, particularly how it assigns responsibility of the scandal. Several crypto industry figures argue that it softens the culpability of Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison while casting Zhao — widely known as CZ — as an outsized villain. Zhao criticized the series in a post on X , calling it "insane" and questioning whether the show was intended to influence public perception. He declined to comment to CNBC beyond his social-media posts. Zhao pleaded guilty in 2023 to failing to maintain an effective anti-money laundering program at Binance, in violation of the U.S. Bank Secrecy Act, in a case separate from the FTX fraud. He was sentenced to four months in prison in 2024 and pardoned by President Donald Trump in October 2025. FTX filed for bankruptcy in November 2022 after a liquidity crisis exposed deep financial problems at the exchange. Investigations later found that billions of dollars in customer funds had been diverted to Alameda Research . Shortly before FTX's collapse, Zhao announced that Binance would liquidate its remaining holdings of FTT, FTX's native token, intensifying pressure on the exchange. Bankman-Fried was sentenced to 25 years in prison in March 2024 after being convicted of fraud and conspiracy charges. Ellison pleaded guilty to fraud and conspiracy, and later cooperated with prosecutors, according to the Justice Department. Crypto commentator Kaleo wrote on X that the series portrayed Bankman-Fried and Ellison as having been pressured and groomed by Zhao into committing their alleged crimes, while casting Zhao as the figure who orchestrated the scandal. "Whoever wrote this script is shameless," Kaleo added. He identifies himself as a co-founder of NFT project LedgArt. Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin said in a reply on X that the show exaggerated Zhao's accent to the point of raising questions about whether the portrayal was racist. Meanwhile, Tigran Gambaryan, a former Binance executive and U.S. federal agent, commented on LinkedIn that the series downplayed Bankman-Fried's responsibility while portraying Zhao as a "cartoonish villain," undermining the showrunners' credibility. Binance co-founder Yi He criticized the series for portraying its characters as "one-dimensional" and "stereotyped," while suggesting that it shifted blame away from those responsible for FTX's collapse. She compared the show unfavorably with Chinese short-form drama platform Hongguo, saying Netflix "might as well be canceled." Changpeng Zhao, co-founder of Binance Holdings Ltd., during the Bitcoin Asia conference in Hong Kong, China, on Thursday, Aug. 27, 2026. Chan Long Hei | Bloomberg | Getty Images But the reactions were not uniformly supportive of Zhao. In a post on X , OKX founder Star Xu said that rather than dismissing criticism as coordinated attacks by competitors, Zhao should respond with facts and evidence. Xu was responding to a post questioning whether accounts defending Zhao were part of a bot network. The eight-episode drama stars Anthony Boyle as FTX founder Sam Bankman-Fried, Julia Garner as former Alameda Research CEO Caroline Ellison and Terry Chen as Zhao. Netflix did not respond to a request for comment. In an interview published by Netflix before the series' release, Graham Moore, the show's creator and co-showrunner, said he encouraged the actors to develop fully three-dimensional characters rather than simply imitate the real-life figures they portrayed. Speaking to Business Insider, Moore said, "I can never prove what was going on in the hearts or minds of Sam's friends when they made those decisions." Moore said he drew on extensive research into the real-life figures' backgrounds and public statements to imagine what may have driven the fractures between them. "The story we're telling is not a financial story, and it's not a crypto story. It's a deeply personal story," he added. Netflix legal disputes While criticism of "The Altruists" has so far unfolded largely on social media, Netflix has previously faced defamation lawsuits over dramatizations of real-life events, including "Inventing Anna" and "Baby Reindeer." Rachel DeLoache Williams, a former Vanity Fair photo editor, sued Netflix in 2022 over her portrayal in "Inventing Anna," a series about convicted fraudster Anna Sorokin. Williams alleged that the show used her real name and personal details while falsely depicting her as greedy, dishonest and disloyal, including portraying her as exploiting her friendship with Sorokin for financial gain. The lawsuit was dismissed in February 2026 after the parties reached a settlement. Netflix and Williams' attorney reportedly confirmed the settlement in separate statements, saying, "Williams and Netflix have resolved the lawsuit." In 2024, Fiona Harvey, who said she inspired the character Martha in "Baby Reindeer," sued Netflix for at least $170 million. Harvey alleged that the series falsely portrayed her as a convicted stalker who had served time in prison and sexually assaulted the show's creator, Richard Gadd. The case is reportedly scheduled to go to trial in May 2027. "We intend to defend this matter vigorously and to stand by Richard Gadd's right to tell his story," Netflix said in a statement reported by the Associated Press. She also challenged the show's claim to be based on a true story and alleged that viewers were able to identify her as the character depicted. In this article TATASTEEL-IN Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT A general view of Tata Steel steelworks on March 27, 2018 in Port Talbot, United Kingdom. Matthew Horwood | Getty Images Tata Steel , one of the world's leading steel producers, on Monday said it will buy a 26.4% stake in India's largest structural steel pipe and tube maker, APL Apollo , for 155.1 billion rupees ($1.67 billion). The acquisition will boost Tata Steel's downstream integration to around 53% from 35%, the company said in a stock exchange filing. That will lead to more value addition, improved product mix, and greater exposure to higher-margin downstream segments, it said. Investors reacted negatively to the deal, with shares of Tata Steel sliding over 9% on Monday, while APL Apollo's stock crashed more than 19% . While the deal is likely to be positive in the long term, the complex structure and lack of clarity have rattled investors, Deven Choksey, founder and managing director of wealth management firm DRChoksey FinServ, told CNBC. As per Tata Steel, before acquiring APL Apollo, it will sell its steel tubes business and Tata Steel Colors to APL Apollo for 280 billion rupees. "APL Apollo will initially fund the acquisition through a mix of acquisition financing and subsequently replace the debt with long-term capitalization," Tata Steel said. "The deal is appearing very complex," said Choksey, adding that minority investors have not been given any clarity or taken into consideration while signing this deal. Tata Steel will hold an investor call, post-market hours on Monday. APL Apollo said after the deal it plans to more than double the downstream capacity to 15.5 million tons from the current 7.5 million tons, making it a leading global downstream steel firm. This capacity addition will be completed by 2035 and would include around 9 million tons per annum of steel tubes and around 6.5 million tons per annum of color-coated products, as per Tata Steel. Tata Steel will acquire a stake from existing shareholders of APL Apollo for 2,100 rupees per share and will ​also make an open offer to acquire an additional 26% ‌stake for 2,301.40 rupees a piece. If the open offer is successful, Tata Steel would get a controlling stake of 52.38% in APL Apollo. World's second-largest steel maker ArcelorMittal was also reportedly in the fray to acquire APL Apollo. The acquisition of APL Apollo would "create a downstream powerhouse for the future" that will serve the growing Indian market, T V Narendran, chief executive and managing director of Tata Steel, said in the release. Tata Steel, which has an annual crude steel capacity of over 35 million tons per annum, is one of the world's most geographically diversified steel producers with presence across India, Europe and Thailand . headlines.article_text: Stocks moving the most today: Live updates Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Visual China Group | Getty Images Shares of CoreWeave and Oracle surged Monday, after the return of Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO gave the artificial intelligence trade new life to start the week. Zscaler also jumped in early trading Monday on the back of a major deal with CrowdStrike. Follow below as CNBC highlights the biggest stock moves of the day. 17 Min Ago CoreWeave, Oracle surge on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang return Shares of CoreWeave and Oracle jumped 20% and 12%, respectively, following the announcement that Jensen Huang was returning as Nvidia CEO. The companies, as well as neoclouds like Nebius and IREN , were among the hardest hit after Huang's resignation ignited fears about Nvidia's role in financing AI companies . The company, known as the "central bank of AI," had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, according to its last quarterly financial filing in July. Oracle lost 10% in the last month, while CoreWeave sank 13%. Nebius and IREN lost 37% and nearly 40%, respectively, during that time. Nebius rose 29% and IREN gained 27% on Monday. — Michelle Fox 1 Hour Ago Nvidia surges after reinstating Huang as CEO Shares of Nvidia surged 28% in premarket trading after the company reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO . Huang stepped down Nov. 12 amid an adultery scandal, sending the stock plummeting and igniting fears over the artificial intelligence trade. Nvidia is down 40.5% in the past month. — Michelle Fox 2 Hours Ago General Motors moves higher after report on Barra successor CEO and Chair of General Motors Mary Barra delivers a speech during the brand's annual technology event in New York on Oct. 21, 2026. Charly Triballeau | AFP | Getty Images Shares of General Motors added more than 2% following a Bloomberg report that said executive Sterling Anderson is being considered as a potential successor to CEO Mary Barra. The company's board wants the next leader to have an expertise in software and self-driving technology, Bloomberg said, citing people familiar with the board's thinking. Anderson came to GM in June 2025, leaving behind the self-driving vehicle technology startup he co-founded, Aurora Innovation. Prior to that he was the director of autopilot programs at Tesla. — Michelle Fox 3 Hours Ago Dollar General rises on upgrade A Dollar General store in Denver, Colorado, US, on Wednesday, Aug. 26, 2026. Chet Strange | Bloomberg | Getty Images Shares of Dollar General moved 2% higher on the back of an upgrade to overweight from neutral at Piper Sandler. Analyst Peter Keith said comparable sales growth and margin expansion should help the discount retailer reach a high-teens earnings-per-share compound annual growth rate over the next three years. Plus, the company's steady growth profile is appealing in an increasingly volatile market environment, he said. — Michelle Fox 3 Hours Ago LuxExperience pops after JPMorgan upgrade JPMorgan upgraded the luxury digital retailer to overweight from neutral on Monday, sending U.S.-listed shares up 6.6% in premarket trading. The bank, which recently hosted a fireside chat with LuxExperience CEO Michael Klinger at a Paris conference, said the company is favorably positioned at the intersection of luxury and e-commerce. It is "notably emerging as the last man standing within an increasingly fragmented and consolidating competitive landscape, with $1B+ of market share opportunity, in our view, over the next 12-24 months across the portfolio," analyst Matthew Boss said in a note Monday. — Michelle Fox 3 Hours Ago Mara, Strategy jump as crypto rebounds Shares of Mara Holdings and Strategy popped 7.6% and 8.5%, respectively, as bitcoin tried to recover some of the steep losses suffered last week. Bitcoin was last up 1.1% at $61,291.08. The flagship cryptocurrency last week traded below $60,000 for the first time since July. headlines.article_text: CrowdStrike to buy Zscaler in $44B deal as AI supercharges cyberattacks Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points CrowdStrike agreed to acquire network security provider Zscaler in an all-stock deal valued at $43.9 billion. The deal is expected to close during the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal year 2028. Cybersecurity vendors have been on an acquisition spree to keep pace with AI-powered threats. In this article CRWD ZS Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 4:05 04:05 Dan Ives: This is just the start of a golden age for cybersecurity Morning Call CrowdStrike plans to buy Zscaler for $43.9 billion in an all-stock deal that combines two significant security businesses at a time when artificial intelligence is supercharging attacks. Shares of CrowdStrike dropped roughly 5% in early trading Monday, while Zscaler surged more than 20%. The deal is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal year 2028. Under the agreement, Zscaler shareholders will receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each share. CrowdStrike's acquisition pushes the Austin-based cyber vendor into the network security market and comes amid a massive year for cybersecurity dealmaking in the wake of high-profile hacks like Hugging Face. "With Zscaler, we're building cybersecurity's operating system: a single control plane to deploy AI, control AI, and enable any agentic application to run safely," CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz said in a statement. "We see a path to become the largest AI safety and security company the world has ever seen." Recent outages affecting Microsoft, the Federal Aviation Administration and JPMorgan Chase have sparked anxiety as businesses accelerate software patching and upgrades to aging systems in an effort to prevent bad actors from exploiting software vulnerabilities with AI. CrowdStrike has been a major beneficiary of skyrocketing demand for AI security, with shares soaring about 80% this year as of Monday's open. Zscaler shares are up about 5% year to date after Monday's surge. Their combined market value exceeded $265 billion as of Friday's close, behind market leader Palo Alto Networks at $282 billion. The deal marks CrowdStrike's biggest acquisition to date and is among the largest in the sector as businesses consolidate and ramp up defenses to fend off AI-powered attacks. Last year, Google announced plans to acquire Wiz for $32 billion. In 2024 Cisco shelled about $28 billion for Splunk. Competitor Palo Alto Networks has also spent billions on several cyber and AI businesses, including startup Applied Compute and a $25 billion deal for CyberArk, which it closed earlier this year. Analysts view the Zscaler deal as a major AI security opportunity, allowing CrowdStrike to capture more customer security spending and close a significant gap with Palo Alto. "The addition of ZS to CRWD's platform could bring more breadth in an era of vendor consolidation and, more importantly, network security to position the company more effectively for rising demand for AI Sovereignty," wrote analysts at JPMorgan. CrowdStrike on Monday also reported better-than-expected fiscal third-quarter results , including earnings of 34 cents per share on $1.58 billion in revenue. That topped the 31 cents per share on $1.53 billion in revenue forecast by LSEG. Zscaler's fiscal first-quarter earnings , also released on Monday, likewise surpassed estimates.
